newsitem.title: UK: Diana says sorry over IRA film outing.
newsitem.headline: Diana says sorry over IRA film outing.

text.p: Princess Diana apologised on Monday for taking Princes William and Harry to a film which critics say glamorises an IRA killer.
The princess said she was unaware of the subject matter of the film "The Devil's Own".

Diana was criticised both for persuading cinema staff to admit 12-year-old Prince Harry to a movie restricted to people aged 15 or over and for taking her sons to see the film, which news reports say has been condemned by its stars Brad Pitt and Harrison Ford.
Pitt has been quoted as describing it as "the most irresponsible bit of film-making - if you can even call it that - that I've ever seen".

A statement from the princess's office at Kensington Palace said: "Diana, Princess of Wales, was unaware of the subject matter of the film 'The Devil's Own', which she saw yesterday with Princes William and Harry.
"She apologises for any distress which may have been caused by her taking her sons to see this film."

The Daily Mail said the princess pleaded with cinema staff to let the under-age Prince Harry into the performance. Prince William met the limit by just one day, having celebrated his 15th birthday on Saturday.
The royal cinema visit came less than a week after the Irish Republican Army killed two policemen in Northern Ireland.
Diana's former husband, royal heir Prince Charles, lost his favourite uncle, Lord Mountbatten, in a killing in 1979 carried out by the IRA, which aims to end British rule of Northern Ireland.
The film, whose opening scene is of a father being shot in front of his children, opened last week after its release was delayed to avoid the British general election campaign.
